description: The Jicamarca Radio Observatory of the Geophysical Institute of Peru is the main equatorial station of the chain of incoherent scatter radio observatories studying the ionosphere and upper atmosphere, and its research covers aeronomy and space weather and meteors and space objects. Its database page links the measurements of the main radar and of the network of geophysical instruments it runs, in three tables: the main databases, mostly ionospheric radar data, including incoherent scatter radar oblique and perpendicular modes (electron density, temperatures, drifts), JULIA drifts and spectra, bistatic measurements, radar imaging, AMISR14, Digisonde ionograms, SIMONE and an HF system; other instruments such as magnetometers, Fabry–Pérot interferometers and atmospheric radars; and models and related databases such as plasma drift models and the Kp index. Links go to the Jicamarca Madrigal database, which holds the ionospheric parameters measured by the radar, to raw data mirrors and to partner archives at Cornell, the University of Illinois and UMass Lowell, and the site also offers real-time pages and the LISN network. Access is free online; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: data sits across several linked archives, and some modes have no database. Coverage is Peru and the equatorial ionosphere. It supports hazard exposure analysis of space weather effects on GNSS and HF radio at low latitudes; related records are the CEDAR Madrigal database and the LAMP Argentine space weather data.
